api-errors.reason: ThalovantApiError.httpFailure in Sources/ThalovantSDK/Errors.swift, which every non-2xx answer ThalovantControlPlane.requestData receives goes through, parses the body once into problem, errorCode and the whole detail, and leaves the bounded message as it was. binary.reason: HiveWire.decodeBinaryFrame reads WIRE-1: four bits of payload type, then the clip itself, never parsed or inflated. The Noise framing marks each frame JSON or not and a binary one was refused outright, so every such frame was unreachable; onBinary delivers it now. Run against the shared binary vectors and against binary-frames.json, which is hivemind-bus-client's own encoder output rather than frames this SDK built for itself.

connection-admission.reason: waitForAdmission in Sources/ThalovantSDK/Connections.swift follows BootstrapIdentityResult.operation: ready and 404 and no operation are admitted, a 5xx is ridden out, failed and timed_out throw ThalovantAdmissionFailedError(errorCode:), and the deadline throws ThalovantAdmissionTimeoutError, which conforms to both ThalovantConnectionFailure and ThalovantTimeoutFailure -- Swift's errors are value types, so the two protocols are how it is both. A links.self on another origin is refused unfetched. Run against the shared connection-admission vectors over URLSession.

connection-kinds.reason: CreateClientIdentityOptions(connectionType:) sends spec.connection_type; createClientIdentity in Sources/ThalovantSDK/ControlPlane.swift checks the echo and, through requireConnectionType in Sources/ThalovantSDK/Connections.swift, deletes a connection made of another kind before failing. Refusals are ThalovantApiError told apart by kind (.unsupportedConnectionType, .plan, .alreadyLinked(clientId:), .auth), read in Sources/ThalovantSDK/Errors.swift from the status and problem. deleteClient reads the etag first, retries once on 412 and counts 404 as deleted. Run against the shared connection-kinds vectors over URLSession.

runtime.reason: Applicable public behavior is implemented and exercised by the named regression suites and shared fixtures. HiveMind #251/#252 only changes the Python upstream client dispatcher; this consumer uses native single-dispatch transports (MCP delegates to the Node SDK), or caller-owned frame parsing in embedded C. No Python HiveMind bus dependency or slave-protocol reinjection exists here. Python now requires fixed upstream 1.1.9a1 and removes its identity-based suppression; equal independent native frames remain distinct. Reply claim metadata follows the Python string-ID contract, with first-seen ordering, case-sensitive fallback stages and legacy unstamped success. Invalid non-string stamps are ignored. Embedded C exposes bounded extraction and claim classification while its caller retains ordered IDs.
